edges.description: In the collecting duct the lost activity is the acid-secreting step itself.
In the inner ear the same pump maintains endolymph pH, so its loss acts there independently of anything happening in the kidney.
Retained acid titrates plasma bicarbonate, and the compensatory distal sodium handling drives potassium loss.
Bone and stone consequences follow from sustained systemic acidosis rather than from the pump defect acting locally.
intermediate_mechanisms: Chronic acidosis mobilises bone carbonate as buffer, causing demineralisation.

Acidosis raises urinary calcium while lowering urinary citrate, and citrate is itself an inhibitor of calcium precipitation, so both the stone-forming load and the protection against it move the wrong way.

edges.description: The route from disturbed endolymph pH to enlarged endolymphatic compartments and cochlear dysfunction is not established in detail; the association is firm, the intermediate steps are not.

edges.description: Reproduces the auditory phenotype and its structural correlate.
edges.limitations: Strain-dependent, which is the substantive caveat rather than a formality: moving the same mutation onto a C57BL/6J background abolished the inner-ear phenotype entirely. What the model demonstrates is therefore conditional on modifier background, and a mapped Chr 13 locus accounts for only about a fifth of the threshold variance, so most of the modifying genetics remains unidentified.

edges.description: The renal branch is not reproduced. The mice alkalinise their urine, showing the pump defect is present and doing something, but they do not develop the systemic acidosis that defines the human disease.
edges.limitations: This is a species difference with an identified mechanism rather than an unexplained failure: B2-containing H+-ATPase complexes, normally confined to intracellular organelles, relocalise to the apical membrane of intercalated cells in B1-deficient mice and substitute for the missing subunit. Human patients evidently do not compensate to the same degree. Any therapeutic strategy tested in these mice for the renal phenotype is therefore being tested in an animal that has already compensated.

edges.description: Hearing is normal in this model despite the gene being knocked out.
edges.limitations: The failure is background-dependent rather than intrinsic to the gene disruption, as the MRL mutant demonstrates. Read together, the two models say that whether Atp6v1b1 loss produces deafness in a mouse depends on modifier genes - which is a caution about using either strain as the reference model, and a candidate explanation for why hearing loss varies so much between human patients with comparable variants.

nodes.description:
A combination controlled-release potassium bicarbonate and potassium citrate preparation, approved in Europe. Its value is adherence rather than a new mechanism: conventional alkali must be taken several times daily including overnight to hold the correction, and this formulation allows less frequent dosing.

It is curated separately from generic alkali because it is a named, regulator-approved product for this indication rather than a class, and because the dosing interval is the practical obstacle to treating a lifelong condition that begins in infancy.

evidence.snippet: ADV7103 is a combination controlled-release potassium bicarbonate and potassium citrate medication approved in Europe that allows less frequent dosing.

nodes.description: Loss of the B1 subunit of the V1 cytosolic domain of the vacuolar H+-ATPase. B1 is one of the few V-ATPase subunits whose expression is essentially restricted to kidney and inner ear, which is precisely why a defect in it produces a two-organ disease rather than a systemic one - the ubiquitous pumps elsewhere use a different B isoform and are unaffected.

nodes.description:
Oral alkali - bicarbonate or citrate salts - given to correct the systemic acidosis the kidney cannot correct itself. Citrate preparations do double duty, since urinary citrate is also the inhibitor of calcium precipitation that is depleted in this disease, so replacing it addresses both the acidosis and the stone risk.
It corrects the consequence, not the cause: the pump remains defective and the urine remains inappropriately alkaline. It also does nothing for the ear, because the auditory branch is not downstream of the acidosis.

nodes.description: The original targeted knockout. It fails to reproduce either half of the human phenotype convincingly - compensated acidosis rather than overt acidosis, and normal hearing - which is what made the spontaneous MRL mutant above worth reporting.

GeneReviews lists potassium-sparing diuretics among the agents to use with caution or avoid. This is counterintuitive at first sight, because the disease runs with hypokalemia and a potassium-sparing agent looks corrective - but the defect is in distal proton secretion, which these drugs impair further, so the acidosis worsens while the potassium is being chased.

evidence.snippet: Agents/circumstances to avoid: Potassium-sparing diuretics should be used with caution or avoided.

nodes.description: The endolymph of the inner ear is an unusual extracellular fluid whose ionic and pH composition must be actively maintained, and the same B1-containing pump does that maintenance. This is the second, independent branch of the disease - it is not a consequence of acidosis, and patients can have it with the renal phenotype barely apparent.

nodes.description: Amplification or cochlear implantation as the hearing loss progresses. Curated as a separate treatment from alkali therapy because it addresses a separate branch of the disease - correcting the acidosis has no effect on the ear. The serial audiometry that decides when to escalate is curated under diagnosis#Audiologic Assessment, so this record covers the intervention rather than the monitoring.

Normal-anion-gap metabolic acidosis with hypokalaemia. The chronic acid load is then buffered at the expense of bone mineral and shifts urinary chemistry toward stone formation, which is how a transport defect in one cell type ends up causing rickets and nephrocalcinosis.

nodes.description: The collecting duct cannot acidify the tubular lumen, so acid generated by metabolism is retained. The signature is an inappropriately alkaline urine in the face of systemic acidosis - the urine pH will not fall below roughly 5.3 no matter how acidotic the blood becomes, which is what distinguishes a distal tubular defect from other causes of acidosis.

nodes.description: A spontaneous Atp6v1b1 mutation arising in an MRL/MpJ colony. It reproduces the ear half of the human disease and not the kidney half - profound hearing impairment with enlarged endolymphatic compartments, but alkaline urine without overt metabolic acidosis.

Calcium deposition in the renal parenchyma with stone formation, and rickets or osteomalacia with growth failure. These are the manifestations that untreated disease accumulates over time, and the ones alkali therapy is given to prevent.
